A field guide to focused reading

The web gives us access to more information than we can reasonably read. Finding the important passages should feel effortless.

Training a useful model

The model is trained with human feedback to identify important information. It achieves 92 percent accuracy on the evaluation dataset.

Training requires eight GPUs and takes three days to complete. The experiment uses a held-out evaluation set to measure generalization.

The objective is to preserve the author's original words while helping readers focus. Each prediction is a typed score with a separate confidence value.

Installation

Install the package with the command below and start the local development server. The API key must remain on the server and must never be included in extension code. 

npm install jev-lens
npm run dev

Open the Chrome extension settings and load the unpacked build folder. Refresh an existing page before opening the side panel for the first time.

Results and limitations

The model achieves strong results on articles and technical documentation. Important warnings and instructions are highlighted alongside the main claims.

The system cannot read images or canvas-only editors without OCR. Complex PDF layouts may have imperfect reading order, so always verify a passage in its original context.

Paragraph mode uses fewer inference units than sentence mode. Actual token usage is measured for every request rather than estimated from page length.
